svg.title: IC and strong rho preserve the same signed-Frobenius coefficient invariant
svg.desc: The same exact field has 83 F2 coordinates and the prime-order subgroup has one scalar dimension over Z/rZ. IC uses 600 formal factor-log coefficients. Strong rho tracks two formal state coefficients a and b for P=aG+bQ. Signed Frobenius transports either labeling by epsilon lambda to the k. IC recovers the target scalar from a factor-log dot product; rho recovers it from a distinguished-point collision with a nonzero denominator. Both require independent dG=Q replay. This is an algebraic comparison without any timing claim.
svg.text: The same invariant, two coefficient systems
83 F₂ field coordinates · one scalar dimension in the prime-order subgroup · λ = 2998004823950457
C = ε τᵏ(P) = [ε λᵏ]P · forward phase transport on the same exact group
IC / 600 FORMAL FACTOR-LOG COLUMNS
v(P) ∈ (Z/rZ)⁶⁰⁰
v(C) = ε λᵏ v(P)
For P = Rⱼ: v(P) = eⱼ; Lⱼ = log_G(Rⱼ).
Root-index extraction yields a four-point
witness and its coefficient vector v_Q.
d = v_Q · L (mod r)
Full rank/log preparation transcript remains absent.
STRONG RHO / TWO FORMAL STATE SCALARS
P = [a]G + [b]Q
(a,b) → (ε λᵏa, ε λᵏb)
Equal canonical collision points imply
(a₁ − a₂) + (b₁ − b₂)d = 0 (mod r).
d = (a₂ − a₁) / (b₁ − b₂) (mod r)
Requires b₁ − b₂ ≠ 0; zero gives no scalar.
Two labels do not mean a two-dimensional subgroup.
Independent final-answer replay: [d]G = Q
Same algebraic transport does not imply the same work or runtime. Source: verification/INVARIANTS.md.
